title: What the Kernel is told about required Lenses, Roles and limits.

deterministic.description: Each deterministic Lens: its name, the exact name of the check run GitHub reports for it, and the id of the one App whose check it is read from. tools/check_authority.py refuses a Lens or a check named twice

check.description: The check run's name exactly as GitHub reports it. The Kernel matches a check in the facts to this Lens by its name, exactly, never by the Lens's own name

workflow.description: For a Lens GitHub Actions runs, the path of its workflow file; null for a Lens no workflow runs. GitHub Actions is one App for every job in the repo, one a pull request adds among them, so a check under the Lens's name from any other path is not the Lens's. The pin is to the path, not to what the file says. tools/check_workflows.py refuses null for a Lens whose App is GitHub Actions, and holds the file to running the Lens's check

status_on_item.description: The one name of the check run the Controller posts as the status on the item. tools/check_authority.py refuses a required Lens's name: the status would speak for that Lens

check_conclusions.description: What each conclusion GitHub gives a required check means, by its own name. A conclusion the map does not name is unreadable. Only success passes: any other name maps to failing, pending or unreadable.

acceptance_reporters.description: For each kind of criterion a check reports, the required deterministic Lens whose check alone may report its result, by the Lens's name, or null where no check may yet: a result for a criterion of that kind is then unreadable. A criterion of kind human is passed by a person's approval alone, and is not named here

max_path_length.description: The longest path of a workflow file a Decision's evidence shows. A longer one, or one not in the form a Lens's workflow takes, is shown as unreadable

max_unnamed_run_seconds.description: How long a counted Run may be listed without its run-name before it is no Run waiting for its name, in seconds: inside it an unidentified Run defers every admission (decision 0036); past it, it defers nothing and is one alert, by its run id (issue 270). P-17 saw a name listed within 3.7 s

issues.description: Which issues the Factory serves, and whose labels count on them (design §4.1, the issue Lifecycle). Each null fails closed: with no date no issue is served, and with no App declared for a label only a person's counts. The Maintainer turns issues on

served_from.description: An issue whose present life began before this time is not served

left_out_labels.description: An issue that carries any of these labels is not served

left_out_types.description: An issue of any of these types is not served

label_apps.description: The name of the one Factory App whose factory:triage, and whose factory:ready, counts beside a person's

intents.description: For each Intent the Kernel admits on an issue, the Role that runs it and that Role's App, or null, which admits nothing. No two Intents name one Role: the readiness Role never judges its own investigation. Every Intent is null until the Maintainer turns it on

app.description: The name of the Role's App, whose comment or label stands in for its Run once the run record has expired
